sources.quote: "Stress normally occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word. In (161) and (162), this can be seen from the fact that when a word is augmented, stress shifts to the right: /a'waro/ 'parrot', /awa'ro:di/ 'little parrot' ... Only on words ending the glottal stop or in a nasalized plosive (cf. 2.3.1), stress falls on the last syllable" (Haude 2006:46, section 2.8.1)

sources.quote: 'Stress (not represented orthographically) occurs by default on the penultimate syllable of the word. When the penultimate syllable is open, it is lengthened ... Syllables with glottal(ized) coda consonants attract stress. Hence, words ending in /p/, /t/ or /k/, glottalized in coda position, are stressed on the last syllable, e.g. /kuː'ɗup/ 'flea', /tʃuː'hat/ 'motacú', /me'ɾek/ 'big'.' Also: Spanish loans adapted to penultimate stress; internal cliticization shifts stress to the new penult.
sources.locator: §2 'Phonology', author-ms pp.1-2 (HAL PDF pp.2-3; the text layer)
sources.note: Most recent statement by the grammar's author; restates penultimate default and frames the final-stress class as 'glottal(ized) coda consonants attract stress' -- useful wording for the record's caution/heavy field. downloaded now (HAL author ms).
